title: Pour Over Ceramic - Coffee Dripper Ceramic Coffee Maker with 3 Holes Flat Bottom, Porcelain Slow Filter Cone for Travel, Camping, Office, Home, Coffee Maker Brew, Pink
reviews: I've been using this for over 3 years to make my morning pour over coffee. I generally use a #2 filter and use enough coffee to make 2 separate cups. I like the fact that it is ceramic and not a plastic version. It works well for me and seems to make a better tasting cup of coffee than the plastic versions that I had used in the past. Also, I have read that some people prefer a pour over maker with 1 hole instead of 3 at the bottom to perhaps concentrate the flavor more. I believe the 3 hole design is fine. One tip though is to pour your boiling water into the coffee slowly and not too fast. Otherwise it could perhaps drain too quickly and dilute the flavor. But I like the fact that the 3 hole design doesn't clog up like the 1 hole design can do. My opinion.

I was getting tired of the whole espresso machine clean up, so I got this little mug-like drip cup to make myself a simple single cup of coffee. I like to use an espresso grind of decaf Lavazza and this works brilliantly and more quickly than I had thought it would. Get your self some Melita coffee filters, your favorite coffee and you're in business without the expense of individual disposable cups that are bad for the environment. Now I put a large pyrex measuring cup of water in the microwave and when it's hot, I pour it a bit at a time into the filter and Voila! A perfect cup, as hot as a want, and then a little almond milk foam from my little frother and when I'm done, just toss the filter with the grounds in the trash. It makes as good a latte as my espresso machine. Love it! It fits right on top of my narrow mugs and my regular sized mugs. It's heavy enough not to wobble as you pour the water into it. I couldn't be any happier with this super simple method. If you travel and can get pretty hot tap water, you can make your own brew. I had a plastic version of this many years ago, so I was familiar with the method, but this ceramic version is much sturdier and more attractive.

Really happy with this ceramic pour over dripper. It feels solid and well made, and the flat bottom with the three holes gives a nice, even brew. Very easy to use and clean, and it makes a great cup of coffee every time. I use it almost daily and it’s been working perfectly. Definitely a great value and a solid choice for pour over coffee.

Cute -- but the base is only 4", so if you have any coffee mugs that are also 4" (or larger), the base will not be sitting solidly on top (see photo). That said, it's cute, I love the color, and it drips slow enough to make a great cup of coffee. I may have someone make a wooden gasket / platform so I can use it with my larger mugs. I'm getting rid of all the plastic in my kitchen, and I do like these. Just wish it was a little wider on the base. It works fine on my mugs that are under 4". I use a #4 cone filter, so the grounds never get a chance to migrate into the cup, so that's why it's so tall compared to the ceramic. (The last one that came too small like this, I repurposed it as a kitchen sink planter for a little plant, because it has built in drainage, and I love these for that use too!)
It's heavy ceramic. I haven't used it yet, but it's very sturdy and I'm sure it will be fine. Pretty aqua color.

I am the only coffee drinker in the house so a pot makes no sense. This is the perfect solution - sits on my tumber or a mug, stays put, super easy to clean, and makes a good cup of coffee. All the benefits of a French press without the mess - used paper filter just pops out, wash, and it's ready to use again. Great value for money. I use water from an electric kettle with a couple small scoops of ground coffee and it's quick and delicious.
This works well for making my morning coffee. Perfect fit for size 2 filters. I love the color, which is perfect for the beach and coffee loving mermaids
Perfect for using up old K-cups after getting rid of your Keurig.
